scope: Current commercial slosh-control examples and their relevance to a GPU SPH demonstration, not a market-wide newest/best ranking.

findings.evidence: The current manufacturer page explicitly describes transverse and longitudinal baffles, alongside a semi-elliptical tank profile.
findings.use_in_project: Recommended final comparison: simplified fixed cross-baffle arrangement in the SAME outer tank as the other cases.
findings.limits: No detailed manufacturer CAD or opening dimensions were obtained. This is a commercial-design-inspired demonstrator, not a replica or validated product performance comparison. The principle predates the page update; do not call it an invention from 2026.
findings.comparison_requirement: Longitudinal plates chiefly address transverse motion, so include a separate prescribed lateral-acceleration diagnostic if explaining this advantage. Straight braking alone cannot establish all-direction superiority.

findings.commercial_example: Carrick 30,000 L general-purpose milk reload tanker
findings.evidence: Manufacturer lists two internal baffles as standard and CIP compatibility.
findings.use_in_project: Evidence that conventional baffles remain part of current commercial designs and that cargo/cleaning requirements affect geometry.
findings.limits: Do not generalize an older regional handbook's unbaffled-milk-tanker description to every current food tanker. No food-hygiene compliance evaluation is proposed.

findings.evidence: Current commercial hollow modules installed through the tank opening; also present in the manufacturer's 2018 catalogue, so not a new 2025 invention.
findings.use_in_project: Optional later example of distributed, multidirectional flow obstruction.
findings.limits: Do not repeat advertised braking-distance reductions as our result. A free packed assembly may move/contact or deform; a fixed porous approximation would need explicit qualification and would not reproduce the product exactly. Not included in the initial four-case simulation.

findings.technology: Seamless mould-in baffles in composite chemical tanks
findings.evidence: Manufacturer specifies seamless Mould in Baffle technology for single-compartment acid tanks and thermoplastic/composite tank construction.
findings.use_in_project: A real commercial manufacturing/material advance for context.
findings.limits: Material, seams, corrosion and structural-life benefits are outside a rigid-wall liquid-only SPH model. Changing only a rendered tank material cannot demonstrate improved slosh damping. Not a separate CFD performance case.

research_context.paper: Liquid sloshing in a tank vehicle: A numerical and experimental investigation with baffle configurations
research_context.evidence_level: Publisher search abstract; full page unavailable in this lookup.
research_context.interpretation: Baffle configuration optimization is an active research topic. A recent paper does not establish production deployment or validate our case.

recommended_story: Principle 1: shorter free-surface spans using separate liquid compartments
Principle 2: through-flow plus dissipation using perforated transverse baffles
Current commercial-style layout: transverse and longitudinal baffles together
claims_policy: Use 'Current commercial design' in the video, not 'world's latest' or 'best'. Preserve measured simulation outcomes without assuming the last design must win.
